predecessors.name: Dumnonia
predecessors.text: the Brittonic kingdom of Dumnonia, of which Cornwall had 'formed part' since the early 6th century

successors.name: Kingdom of England
successors.text: Cornwall west of the Tamar: 14 cells that Cliopatria's England shape gains in 947

ledger.x: 710: the Britons of Dumnonia are left holding Cornwall.
946: Cornwall passes to England on the map.

wars.name: Battle of Hehil
wars.outcome: 'The Annales Cambriae report that in AD 722 the Britons of Cornwall won a battle at Hehil.'

wars.name: Egbert's campaigns in Cornwall
wars.outcome: 815: 'king Ecgbryht raided in Cornwall from east to west' (read as the end of Cornish independence); 825: a battle between the Cornish and the men of Devon at Gafulforda; 838: 'the Cornish and their Danish allies were defeated by Egbert' at Hingston Down.

wars.name: Æthelstan and the Tamar boundary
wars.outcome: William of Malmesbury: Æthelstan expelled the Cornish from Exeter and fixed the boundary at the Tamar; the Cornwall page dates the boundary to 936 and doubts the burning of Exeter.

certainty.note: The only candidate for a sharp line is the Tamar boundary of 936 (Cornwall page), a story the Æthelstan page records sceptical historians doubting; no earlier frontier is dated.
